tasks.title: Node NotReady: kubelet stopped
tasks.question:
ssh cka01001
The worker node node01 is reported as NotReady. Investigate the cause and bring node01 back to the Ready state. Your fix must survive a reboot of node01.
keys: fix must survive reboot (enable the service)
tasks.setup:
ssh node01 'systemctl stop kubelet; systemctl disable kubelet' 2>/dev/null
sleep 60
clear

steps.title: See which node is sick
steps.see:
NAME           STATUS     ROLES           AGE   VERSION
controlplane   Ready      control-plane   ...   ...
node01         NotReady   <none>          ...   ...
steps.why: NotReady usually means the kubelet on that node is not talking. If it still says Ready, wait 30 s and run it again. The control plane waits ~50 s before marking a node NotReady.

steps.title: Log in to node01 and become root
steps.why: The kubelet runs on the node itself, not as a pod. systemctl changes need root. The real exam requires sudo -i. Killercoda is already root, so it changes nothing there.

steps.title: Check the kubelet service
steps.see:
○ kubelet.service - kubelet: The Kubernetes Node Agent
     Loaded: loaded (/usr/lib/systemd/system/kubelet.service; disabled; preset: enabled)   <-- disabled
...
     Active: inactive (dead) ...
steps.why: Shows the kubelet is stopped and will not start at boot. Shortened: ... marks parts of the real output left out.

steps.title: Start it and enable it at boot
steps.see: enabled
steps.why: enable = survives reboot, --now = start right away.

steps.title: Go back and check
steps.see:
NAME           STATUS   ROLES           AGE   VERSION
controlplane   Ready    control-plane   ...   ...
node01         Ready    <none>          ...   ...
steps.why: Two exits: one leaves root, one leaves node01. Wait up to 30s for the node to report Ready.

tasks.beginner: The kubelet on node01 is switched off; turn it on and make it start automatically. Words you need: kubelet = the node agent that starts pods and reports to the control plane.

tasks.title: Service has no endpoints
tasks.question:
ssh cka01002
In namespace shop the Service cart does not forward traffic to the Pods of Deployment cart. Fix the Service so that it routes to the Deployment's Pods. Do not modify the Deployment.
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace shop --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: cart, namespace: shop}
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: cart}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: cart}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - {name: nginx, image: nginx:1.27-alpine, ports: [{containerPort: 80}]}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: cart, namespace: shop}
spec:
  selector: {app: carts}
  ports: [{port: 80, targetPort: 80}]
EOF
clear

steps.title: See the empty endpoints
steps.see:
NAME          ADDRESSTYPE   PORTS   ENDPOINTS   AGE
cart-xxxxx    IPv4          80      <unset>     1m
steps.why: ENDPOINTS <unset> = no Pod IPs: the Service selector matches no Pod.

steps.title: Compare labels and selector
cmds: k get service cart -o wide -n shop
steps.see:
NAME         READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   LABELS
cart-...     1/1     Running   0          2m    app=cart,pod-template-hash=...
cart-...     1/1     Running   0          2m    app=cart,pod-template-hash=...
NAME   TYPE        CLUSTER-IP   EXTERNAL-IP   PORT(S)   AGE   SELECTOR
cart   ClusterIP   10.96...     <none>        80/TCP    2m    app=carts   <-- typo
steps.why: One letter typo in the selector.

steps.title: Fix the selector
steps.see: service/cart patched
steps.why: Point the Service at the real Pod label.

steps.title: Test from inside the cluster
cmds: k run tmp --rm -it --restart=Never --image=busybox:1.36 -n shop -- wget -qO- -T3 cart
steps.see:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
<title>Welcome to nginx!</title>
...
steps.why: A real request proves traffic flows. Shortened: ... marks parts of the real output left out.

tasks.title: Pods stuck Pending (requests too big)
tasks.question:
ssh cka01003
The Pods of Deployment reporter in namespace batch stay Pending. Find the reason and fix it so that all replicas are Running. Set the memory request of the container to 128Mi. Keep the number of replicas unchanged.
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace batch --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: reporter, namespace: batch}
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: reporter}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: reporter}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: reporter
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sh","-c","sleep 3600"]
        resources: {requests: {memory: 64Gi}}
EOF
clear

steps.title: See Pending pods
steps.see:
NAME           READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
reporter-...   0/1     Pending   0          1m
reporter-...   0/1     Pending   0          1m
steps.why: Pending = scheduler cannot find a node.

steps.title: Read the reason
cmds: k describe pods -l app=reporter -n batch | grep -A3 Events
steps.see:
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age   From               Message
  ----     ------            ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling  ...   default-scheduler  0/2 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient memory, 1 node(s) had untolerated taint ...
steps.why: Events tell why a pod is not scheduled. Ignore the taint part (that is the control plane); Insufficient memory is the cause. Shortened: ... marks parts of the real output left out.

steps.title: Lower the request
steps.see: deployment.apps/reporter resource requirements updated
steps.why: Asks for less memory so a node fits.

steps.title: Check
steps.see:
NAME           READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
reporter-...   1/1     Running   0          20s
reporter-...   1/1     Running   0          18s
steps.why: New pods replace the old Pending ones.

tasks.beginner: The pods ask for more memory than any node has; ask for less. Words you need: request = memory a pod reserves up front; scheduler = the part that picks a node with enough free memory.

tasks.title: CrashLoop / restarts: wrong liveness probe
tasks.question:
ssh cka01004
Deployment api in namespace web keeps restarting its Pods. Identify the cause and fix it. The nginx container listens on port 80. Do not delete the Deployment.
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace web --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: api, namespace: web}
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: api}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: api}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:1.27-alpine
        ports: [{containerPort: 80}]
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet: {path: /, port: 8080}
          initialDelaySeconds: 3
          periodSeconds: 3
          failureThreshold: 2
EOF
clear

steps.title: See restarts
steps.see:
NAME      READY   STATUS    RESTARTS     AGE
api-...   1/1     Running   3 (5s ago)   40s   <-- RESTARTS grows (or CrashLoopBackOff)
steps.why: Growing RESTARTS = something kills the container.

steps.title: Read events
cmds: k describe pods -l app=api -n web | grep -i -A2 liveness
steps.see:
Liveness:     http-get http://:8080/ delay=3s timeout=1s period=3s #success=1 #failure=2   <-- 8080
...
  Warning  Unhealthy  ...  kubelet  Liveness probe failed: Get "http://...:8080/": dial tcp ...:8080: connect: connection refused
steps.why: Probe checks port 8080 but nginx uses 80. Shortened: ... marks parts of the real output left out.

steps.title: Fix the probe port
steps.see:
livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /
            port: 80  <-- fix
steps.why: In vim change the probe port 8080 to 80. Esc, :wq, Enter → deployment.apps/api edited. Probe now checks the port nginx really uses. Edit the Deployment, not the Pod.

steps.title: Check
steps.see:
deployment "api" successfully rolled out
NAME      READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
api-...   1/1     Running   0          30s   <-- new pod, RESTARTS 0
steps.why: The NEW pod (new name) shows RESTARTS 0 and stays healthy; the old one disappears.

tasks.docs: Configure Liveness, Readiness and Startup Probes (search: livenessProbe httpGet)
tasks.beginner: The health check knocks on the wrong door (8080) so Kubernetes keeps restarting the pod. Words you need: livenessProbe = a URL the kubelet calls again and again (N failures in a row = container restarted).

tasks.title: Install cri-dockerd + kernel sysctl
tasks.question:
ssh cka01007
Prepare this node for a Docker-based container runtime:
- Install the Debian package /root/cri-dockerd.deb using dpkg.
- Enable and start the cri-docker service.
- Configure these kernel parameters so they persist across reboots (file /etc/sysctl.d/k8s.conf):
  net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables = 1
  net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1
  net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding = 1
  net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 131072
tasks.setup:
test -f /root/cri-dockerd.deb || curl -fsSLo /root/cri-dockerd.deb https://github.com/Mirantis/cri-dockerd/releases/download/v0.3.16/cri-dockerd_0.3.16.3-0.ubuntu-jammy_amd64.deb || echo "download failed - check release page"
ls -l /root/cri-dockerd.deb || echo "MISSING: download a cri-dockerd .deb for your Ubuntu from https://github.com/Mirantis/cri-dockerd/releases to /root/cri-dockerd.deb"
clear

steps.title: Become root
steps.see: -rw-r--r-- 1 root root ... /root/cri-dockerd.deb
steps.why: dpkg, systemctl and /etc need root. The real exam requires sudo -i. Killercoda is already root. If the file is missing on Killercoda, the setup download failed. Download a .deb from the cri-dockerd releases page. Or just practise the commands.

steps.title: Install the package
steps.see:
...
Unpacking cri-dockerd (0.3.16~3-0~ubuntu-jammy) ...
Setting up cri-dockerd (0.3.16~3-0~ubuntu-jammy) ...
steps.why: dpkg installs a local .deb file. If dpkg stops with missing dependencies, run `apt-get -f install -y`. Then check again. Status `iU` means unpacked but not configured yet. `ii` means installed. Shortened: ... marks parts of the real output left out.

steps.title: Enable and start the service
steps.see:
Job for cri-docker.service failed because the control process exited with error code.
...
enabled
steps.why: enable = at boot, --now = start now. Killercoda has no Docker, so the start fails there (first line), but the enable still worked: is-enabled says enabled. In the exam (Docker present) there is no error. Shortened: ... marks parts of the real output left out.

steps.title: Write the sysctl file
cmds:
cat <<'EOF' > /etc/sysctl.d/k8s.conf
net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables = 1
net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1
net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding = 1
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 131072
EOF
steps.why: Files in /etc/sysctl.d survive reboots. Paste the whole block at once, including the final EOF line. Everything between the two EOFs goes into the file.

steps.title: Load the kernel modules now and at every boot
steps.why: bridge-nf-call-iptables only exists when br_netfilter is loaded, nf_conntrack_max needs nf_conntrack. modprobe loads them now. The modules-load.d file loads them after a reboot. So the sysctl settings really persist.

steps.title: Apply the settings now
steps.see:
net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables = 1
net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1
net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding = 1
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 131072
steps.why: Applies all /etc/sysctl.d files without rebooting.

tasks.docs: kubernetes.io: Container Runtimes (search: cri-dockerd, sysctl ip_forward)
tasks.beginner: Install a runtime package and turn on 4 Linux network settings permanently. On Killercoda Docker is absent, so cri-docker will not start. The jammy .deb may not match a newer Ubuntu. dpkg, enable and sysctl still practise. Words you need: sysctl = a Linux kernel setting; kernel module = a driver loaded with modprobe, needed before some sysctl settings exist.

tasks.title: Gateway API: migrate Ingress to Gateway + HTTPRoute
tasks.question:
ssh cka01011
Migrate the existing Ingress web in namespace web-app to the Gateway API, keeping HTTPS:
- Create a Gateway named web-gateway using GatewayClass nginx, with an HTTPS listener on port 443 for hostname gateway.web.example. Use the TLS Secret web-tls already referenced by the Ingress.
- Create an HTTPRoute named web-route bound to web-gateway that sends all paths (/) for gateway.web.example to Service web on port 80.
- Delete the Ingress web when done.
keys: listener HTTPS 443, host gateway.web.example, secret web-tls
delete ingress web at the end
tasks.setup:
kubectl get crd gateways.gateway.networking.k8s.io >/dev/null 2>&1 || kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/v1.2.1/standard-install.yaml
kubectl create namespace web-app --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
openssl req -x509 -nodes -newkey rsa:2048 -days 365 -subj "/CN=gateway.web.example" -keyout /tmp/web-tls.key -out /tmp/web-tls.crt 2>/dev/null
kubectl create secret tls web-tls --cert=/tmp/web-tls.crt --key=/tmp/web-tls.key --dry-run=client -o yaml -n web-app | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: GatewayClass
metadata: {name: nginx}
spec: {controllerName: example.net/gateway-controller}
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: web, namespace: web-app}
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: web}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: web}}
    spec:
      containers: [{name: nginx, image: nginx:1.27-alpine, ports: [{containerPort: 80}]}]
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: web, namespace: web-app}
spec: {selector: {app: web}, ports: [{port: 80, targetPort: 80}]}
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata: {name: web, namespace: web-app}
spec:
  tls: [{hosts: [gateway.web.example], secretName: web-tls}]
  rules:
  - host: gateway.web.example
    http:
      paths:
      - {path: /, pathType: Prefix, backend: {service: {name: web, port: {number: 80}}}}
EOF
clear

steps.title: Read the Ingress you must copy
cmds: k get ingress web -o yaml -n web-app | grep -A15 "^spec"
steps.see:
spec:
  rules:
  - host: gateway.web.example   <-- host
    http:
      paths:
      - backend:
          service:
            name: web
            port:
              number: 80
        path: /
        pathType: Prefix
  tls:
  - hosts:
    - gateway.web.example
    secretName: web-tls   <-- secret
steps.why: Host, TLS secret and backend move to the new objects.

steps.title: Check the GatewayClass
steps.see:
NAME    CONTROLLER                       ACCEPTED   AGE
nginx   example.net/gateway-controller   Unknown    2m
steps.why: Gateway must use an existing class.

steps.title: Create the Gateway
cmds:
cat <<'EOF' > gw.yaml
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata: {name: web-gateway, namespace: web-app}
spec:
  gatewayClassName: nginx
  listeners:
  - name: https
    protocol: HTTPS
    port: 443
    hostname: gateway.web.example
    tls:
      mode: Terminate
      certificateRefs:

    metadata: {labels: {app: apache-server}}

tasks.title: Reuse a retained PV for MariaDB
tasks.question:
ssh cka01016

kind: PersistentVolume
metadata: {name: mariadb-pv}
spec:
  capacity: {storage: 250Mi}
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  storageClassName: ""
  hostPath: {path: /mnt/data/mariadb, type: DirectoryOrCreate}
EOF
cat <<'EOF' > /root/mariadb-deploy.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: mariadb, namespace: mariadb}
spec:
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: mariadb}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: mariadb}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: mariadb
        image: mariadb:11
        env: [{name: MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD, value: cka}]
        volumeMounts: [{name: data, mountPath: /var/lib/mysql}]

      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: ""
EOF
clear

cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: logs-pvc, namespace: storage-fix}
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: fast-ssd
  resources: {requests: {storage: 200Mi}}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: log-writer, namespace: storage-fix}
spec:
  containers:
  - {name: c, image: busybox:1.36, command: [sh, -c, "while true; do date >> /data/log; sleep 5; done"], volumeMounts: [{name: d, mountPath: /data}]}
  volumes: [{name: d, persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: logs-pvc}}]

  Warning  ProvisioningFailed  ...   persistentvolume-controller  storageclass.storage.k8s.io "fast-ssd" not found

cat <<'EOF' > /root/logs-pvc.yaml

kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: logs-pvc, namespace: storage-fix}
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: local-path
  resources: {requests: {storage: 200Mi}}
EOF
steps.see: persistentvolumeclaim/logs-pvc created

persistentvolumeclaim/logs-pvc   Bound    pvc-...  200Mi      RWO            local-path     ...

NAME             READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
pod/log-writer   1/1     Running   0          40s

tasks.title: Static PV + PVC + Pod (hostPath)
tasks.question:
ssh cka02016
Create a PersistentVolume app-pv: 1Gi, ReadWriteOnce, hostPath /srv/app-data, storageClassName manual.
Create a PersistentVolumeClaim app-pvc in namespace app-store requesting 500Mi from class manual.
Create a Pod app-writer (image busybox:1.36, command sleep 3600) in namespace app-store mounting the claim at /data.
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace app-store --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
clear

steps.title: Create PV, PVC and Pod
cmds:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/all.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata: {name: app-pv}
spec:
  capacity: {storage: 1Gi}
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: manual
  hostPath: {path: /srv/app-data}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: app-pvc, namespace: app-store}
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: manual
  resources: {requests: {storage: 500Mi}}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: app-writer, namespace: app-store}
spec:
  containers:
  - {name: c, image: busybox:1.36, command: [sleep, "3600"], volumeMounts: [{name: d, mountPath: /data}]}
  volumes: [{name: d, persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: app-pvc}}]
EOF
steps.see:
persistentvolume/app-pv created
persistentvolumeclaim/app-pvc created
pod/app-writer created
steps.why: cat <<'EOF' > /root/all.yaml ... EOF starts a "heredoc". It writes every line up to EOF into /root/all.yaml. This is the same as pasting into vim. --- separates objects in one file. PV = disk, PVC = request, Pod = user.

steps.title: Check binding
cmds: k get pv app-pv; k get pvc,pods -n app-store
steps.see:
NAME     CAPACITY   ACCESS MODES   RECLAIM POLICY   STATUS   CLAIM               STORAGECLASS   ...
app-pv   1Gi        RWO            Retain           Bound    app-store/app-pvc   manual         ...
NAME                            STATUS   VOLUME   CAPACITY   ACCESS MODES   STORAGECLASS   ...
persistentvolumeclaim/app-pvc   Bound    app-pv   1Gi        RWO            manual         ...

NAME             READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
pod/app-writer   1/1     Running   0          20s
steps.why: The PVC gets the 1Gi PV (bigger is OK). So the PVC also shows CAPACITY 1Gi, the PV's size. Shortened: ... marks parts of the real output left out.

steps.title: Write a test file

steps.see: hi

tasks.title: Gateway API: header match + weighted split
tasks.question:
ssh cka03010
In namespace shop-gw a Gateway shop-gw (HTTP, port 80) and Services shop-v1 and shop-v2 exist.
Create an HTTPRoute named shop-route attached to shop-gw for hostname shop.example.com:
- Requests with header x-version: v2 go 100% to shop-v2.
- All other requests are split 80% shop-v1 and 20% shop-v2.
Both Services listen on port 80.

kubectl get crd gateways.gateway.networking.k8s.io >/dev/null 2>&1 || kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/v1.2.1/standard-install.yaml
kubectl create namespace shop-gw --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: GatewayClass
metadata: {name: cka-demo}
spec: {controllerName: example.net/gateway-controller}
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata: {name: shop-gw, namespace: shop-gw}
spec:
  gatewayClassName: cka-demo
  listeners: [{name: http, protocol: HTTP, port: 80}]
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: shop-v1, namespace: shop-gw}
spec: {selector: {app: shop, v: "1"}, ports: [{port: 80}]}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: shop-v2, namespace: shop-gw}
spec: {selector: {app: shop, v: "2"}, ports: [{port: 80}]}
EOF
clear

steps.title: Check the Gateway
cmds: k get gateway shop-gw -o yaml -n shop-gw | grep -A6 listeners
steps.see:
listeners:
  - allowedRoutes:
      namespaces:
        from: Same
    name: http
    port: 80
    protocol: HTTP
steps.why: Route will attach to this listener (allowedRoutes Same = routes from this namespace).

steps.title: Create the HTTPRoute
cmds:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/route.yaml
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata: {name: shop-route, namespace: shop-gw}
spec:
  parentRefs: [{name: shop-gw}]
  hostnames: [shop.example.com]
  rules:
  - matches:
    - headers: [{name: x-version, value: v2}]
    backendRefs: [{name: shop-v2, port: 80}]
  - matches:
    - path: {type: PathPrefix, value: /}
    backendRefs:
    - {name: shop-v1, port: 80, weight: 80}
    - {name: shop-v2, port: 80, weight: 20}
EOF
steps.see: httproute.gateway.networking.k8s.io/shop-route created
steps.why: cat <<'EOF' > /root/route.yaml ... EOF starts a "heredoc". It writes every line up to EOF into /root/route.yaml. This is the same as pasting into vim. Rule 1 has no path, so it also matches path /. With equal paths, Gateway API picks the rule with more header matches. So x-version: v2 requests go 100% to shop-v2.

steps.title: Check

steps.see:
Rules:
    Backend Refs:
...

      Port:    80
      Weight:  1
    Matches:
      Headers:
        Name:   x-version   <-- rule 1
        Type:   Exact
        Value:  v2
...
      Name:    shop-v1
      Port:    80
      Weight:  80          <-- rule 2
...
      Name:    shop-v2
      Port:    80
      Weight:  20
...

tasks.question:
ssh cka03011
Pods labelled app=api in namespace payments must accept traffic ONLY from Pods labelled app=gateway in namespace edge, on TCP port 80. A default deny-ingress policy exists in payments.

tasks.title: HPA: CPU + memory, scaleUp and scaleDown behavior
tasks.question:
ssh cka03013
Create a HorizontalPodAutoscaler named worker-hpa in namespace metrics-app for Deployment worker:
- min 2, max 6 replicas,
- target 60% average CPU utilisation AND 70% average memory utilisation,
- scale up by at most 2 Pods per 60 seconds,
- scale-down stabilization window of 120 seconds.
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace metrics-app --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: worker, namespace: metrics-app}
spec:
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: worker}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: worker}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - {name: worker, image: nginx:1.27-alpine, resources: {requests: {cpu: 100m, memory: 64Mi}}}
EOF
clear

steps.title: Create the HPA
cmds:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/hpa.yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata: {name: worker-hpa, namespace: metrics-app}
spec:
  scaleTargetRef: {apiVersion: apps/v1, kind: Deployment, name: worker}
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 6
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource: {name: cpu, target: {type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 60}}
  - type: Resource
    resource: {name: memory, target: {type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 70}}
  behavior:
    scaleUp:
      policies:
      - {type: Pods, value: 2, periodSeconds: 60}
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 120
EOF
steps.see: horizontalpodautoscaler.autoscaling/worker-hpa created
steps.why: cat <<'EOF' > /root/hpa.yaml ... EOF starts a "heredoc". It writes every line up to EOF into /root/hpa.yaml. This is the same as pasting into vim. Two metrics: HPA computes replicas for each and uses the higher. scaleUp policy Pods 2 / 60 s = add at most 2 pods per minute. scaleDown stabilizationWindowSeconds 120 = look back 2 min before removing pods. It acts on the highest recommendation of the last 2 min.
